commits.message: feat(sim): mob defs, A* pathfinding, AI state machine, combat and projectiles
test(sim): vitest suites for pathfinding, mob spawn, AI and combat

notes: Scope delivered: packages/sim/src/mob, packages/sim/src/pathfind, packages/sim/src/combat. Nothing outside those trees plus this report was touched; packages/core-types, docs/orchestration, every package.json, root config, CI, and the sim index/shared/ecs/schedule/physics/replay/testing trees are unchanged.

Systems are exported with the SystemFn signature (world, dt, tick) and map to SYSTEM_ORDER as mobSpawn=mobSpawnSystem, mobAi=mobAiSystem, combat=combatSystem, projectile=combatProjectileSystem, despawn=mobDespawnSystem. mobSimSystemEntries() in mob/systems.ts returns them as SystemEntry[] in that order, ready for sim-a to register; no scheduler wiring was done here.

Before any system runs, sim-a must call mobBindContext(world, { voxels, seed, bus }) from mob/context.ts. Systems never call world.flush() themselves, so the scheduler owns flushing, exactly like the other sim subtrees.

Physics boundary respected: AI only writes Intent (forward/strafe/jump/sprint), plus Velocity for knockback and arrow motion. Collision resolution and the movement integration are left to sim-a. ../physics, ../schedule and ../replay are never imported.

Steering is deliberately trig free: mobSteer keeps Intent.yaw at 0 and writes forward as the +Z axis and strafe as the +X axis, scaled by MobDef.speed / PHYSICS.walkSpeed. If the physics integration rotates Intent by Transform.yaw instead of treating it as world aligned, tell me and I will switch mobSteer to emit yaw-relative components; the change is local to mob/ai.ts.

Determinism: every random draw goes through core-types makeRng seeded with (worldSeed, MOB_RNG_SALT.*, tick, attempt). No Math.random, Date.now, or trig in state calculations. The single wall-clock read is the A* maxMillis budget (pathNow, sampled every 64 expansions), which can only change when a search gives up and reports status 'partial'; it never changes node ordering or costs. pathSetClock injects a deterministic clock for replay or tests.

Pathfinding: A* over PATH_DIRS (4 cardinal then 4 diagonal), octile heuristic, binary heap keyed (f, h, insertion) so ties break deterministically. Cut off by PATHFIND.maxNodes and PATHFIND.maxMillis with status 'partial' and the best-so-far route. Diagonals require both orthogonal neighbours to be passable, so corners cannot be cut. Unloaded chunks are passable at PATHFIND.unloadedPenalty rather than solid. Costs come only from MOVE_COST. pathDijkstra shares the same expansion with a zero heuristic and is used by the optimality test.

Mobs: 4 passive (pig, cow, sheep, chicken) and 4 hostile (zombie, skeleton, creeper, spider) mapped to core-types MOB. Spawning honours spawnMaxBlockLight, minDistance, maxDistance, mobCapHostile, mobCapPassive and attemptsPerTick; despawn uses despawnDistance. Combat honours invulnerableTicks, playerMaxHealth, regenIntervalTicks, creeperFuseTicks, creeperRadius, creeperDamage, arrowDamage, arrowSpeed and arrowGravity, with knockback added to Velocity from PHYSICS.knockbackHorizontal and knockbackVertical.

Local tuning constants live beside the code they serve and never shadow a contract value: PATH_JUMP_BLOCKS, PATH_SAFE_FALL_BLOCKS (pathfind/moves.ts), MOB_WAYPOINT_RADIUS, MOB_WANDER_TICKS, MOB_WANDER_ODDS, MOB_FLEE_TICKS (mob/ai.ts), MOB_SPAWN_SURFACE_SCAN, MOB_SPAWN_VERTICAL_SPAN, MOB_SPAWN_GROUP_SPREAD, MOB_SPAWN_HOSTILE_ODDS (mob/spawn.ts) and COMBAT_ARROW_LIFE_TICKS (combat/projectile.ts). Move any of these into the contract if another package needs to agree on them.

Tests: 33 vitest cases in 5 files covering A* optimality against Dijkstra in a fixed maze, the node-budget cutoff returning 'partial', the diagonal corner rule, unloaded ground being expensive rather than impassable, light-gated and deterministic spawning, both mob caps, despawn distance, chase acquisition with chaseStartDistance/chaseStopDistance hysteresis and PATHFIND.repathTicks, melee damage and cooldown, the creeper fuse and explosion, skeleton arrow cadence, passive flee on damage, the invulnerability window, knockback magnitudes, death events, player regen, fall-damage handoff, and arrow ballistics including a wall stop.
head_sha is the commit the four checks were run against. This report is committed on top of it as the branch tip, which changes nothing under packages/.

Check logs were written to /tmp/sim-c-logs/ inside the runner env rather than the repo, because a logs/ directory is outside my owned paths. Use the job_id values above to re-read the captured output.
